executiveSummary: AI compute demand is accelerating sharply — routed tokens hit 717.5T in October, up 26.5% month-on-month, with share rotating toward lower-cost open-weight models as DeepSeek gained 9.6pp and OpenAI shed 3.9pp; simultaneously, H100 cloud rental rates rose 7.9% to $3.88/hr month-to-date, suggesting supply is not keeping pace with demand growth. Taiwan semiconductor supply-chain revenue rose 3.5% month-on-month (Aug '26 → Sep '26), led by Semi Equipment & Consumables at +9.4%, though AI Silicon was flat at -0.1% and Power/DC Electrical fell -3.6% against the broader trend. On the fund-positioning side, 13F data (Q1 '26 → Q2 '26) shows concentrated managers rotating into Software & IT Services (+$21.2B net) and out of Semiconductors (-$3.1B), with TSM the single most-exited consensus name at -0.89pp across five funds all trimming. AI compute list prices continued to deflate (-2.9% QoQ input, Q3 '26 → Q4 '26 QTD), driven almost entirely by DeepSeek's -18.5% cut, while Anthropic and OpenAI held flat — a structural price-vs-volume divergence worth tracking. Hugging Face new Spaces rose 6.9% week-on-week and 41.5% month-on-month, with Data Analysis (+15.9%) and Search & Research (+13.7%) the fastest-growing use cases, confirming that developer build activity remains broadly healthy across the AI stack.

lines.line: CPU average street price fell -0.4% quarter-on-quarter (Q3-26 → Q4-26). Desktop was the largest mover at -0.6%, while Server edged down -0.1% and Laptop was flat at 0.0%. The dashboard carries no explanatory insights beyond the like-for-like PassMark street-price aggregation across Intel and AMD across all three segments.

Taiwan supply-chain revenue rose +3.5% month-on-month (Aug '26 → Sep '26), with 6 of 10 stages firmer; Semi Equipment & Consumables led at +9.4%, followed by Legacy/Mature Node +4.8% and Analog Cycle +4.7%. The standout counter-move was Power/DC Electrical at -3.6%, running against peers clustered around +4.3% — the dashboard flags this as a potential timing effect or genuine turn. At the company level, Alchip accelerated +222ppt year-on-year (AI Silicon, YoY 496%) while Quanta decelerated -101ppt (Rack/ODM, YoY 77%), per the dashboard's acceleration/deceleration breakdown.

AI model input price fell -2.9% quarter-on-quarter (Q3 '26 → Q4 '26 QTD), with output prices down -1.6% over the same period. The move was almost entirely driven by DeepSeek at -18.5%, which also gained +11.76pp of share; OpenAI moved -0.1% and Anthropic held flat at 0.0%. Per the dashboard's notes, list prices are otherwise flat month-to-month — the quarterly reset is the only mechanism for change.

Schneider Electric data-centre equipment prices rose +1.7% month-on-month (14 Sep → 19 Oct) on a Graybar like-for-like basis across 2 solidly-priced categories. UPS was the big mover at +2.6%, while Rack PDUs added +0.3% and Rack Systems +0.1%; Busway/Power Distribution was the only category to soften at -0.3%. The dashboard records no further explanatory insights beyond the category-level price captures.

The median consensus-held name (3+ of 14 watchlist funds) saw its weight trimmed by -0.38pp quarter-on-quarter (Q1 '26 → Q2 '26), with TSM the most-sold at -0.89pp — all 5 holding funds trimmed — and CPNG next at -1.2pp with 3 of 6 holders trimming. On the buy side, V was the clearest consensus add: 8 funds hold it, 6 were adding (+0.42pp average). Sector-rotation flows show $21.2B moved into Software & IT Services and $8.1B into Computers & Hardware, while Semiconductors saw $3.1B in net outflows and Energy $7.8B.

Nu's Brazilian credit-card market share slipped -0.19pp quarter-on-quarter to 15.49% (1Q '26 → 2Q '26), with 4 of 7 issuers gaining share; Banco do Brasil was the biggest loser at -0.52pp. Nu's TPV share, however, held at 23.6% of Brazilian card payment volume (1Q '26, +0.07pp QoQ), running 8.1pp above its balance share — indicating customers spend heavily on the card even where revolving balances are lower. The macro backdrop is deteriorating: BCB data shows system-wide credit-card 90-day NPL at 9.96% (+0.45pp MoM, Aug '26), and Nu's own 90+ NPL reached 6.9% (+0.40pp QoQ in 2Q '26), structurally above incumbents Itaú (1.9%) and Bradesco (4.3%) given Nu's broader credit base.

SAP AI practitioner sentiment rose +0.09 pts month-on-month (Oct '26 → Nov '26) to 2.70/5, with 8 of 9 topics firmer and only S/4HANA AI Features softer at -0.03 pts. The largest single-topic gain was SAP RPT1 at +0.42 pts, driven by SAP-RPT-1.6 reaching general availability through AI Core — though the dashboard's own research notes that genuine customer production deployments are absent and adoption reads as playground-and-pilot rather than production. Business Data Cloud added +0.14 pts, supported by TrustRadius scores of 8.6/10 across 83 ratings and G2 scores of 4.2/5 across 76 reviews, with reviewers crediting zero-copy federation as the key differentiator for SAP-centric data estates.

US passenger throughput was down -1.3% year-on-year (Oct '26 vs Oct '25), running at 2.54M passengers/day per TSA checkpoint data current to 29 Oct '26. Globally, IATA RPK data (latest available Aug '26) shows the Middle East as the sharpest regional decline at -14.6% YoY (9.5% of global RPK, -4.6pp vs prior month), while Latin America led growth at +5.3% YoY; North America was also negative at -2.2% YoY. The dashboard notes that month-to-month raw count swings are seasonal, which is why demand is read year-on-year, and that the IATA regional data operates on a ~2-month reporting lag relative to the TSA headline.

New Hugging Face Spaces rose +6.9% week-on-week (wk 5 Oct → wk 12 Oct) to 6,920 for the week, with Chat & Assistants (+12.6%), Data Analysis (+15.9%), and Search & Research (+13.7%) the fastest-growing use cases; Image Generation was the sole decliner at -5.6%. On a monthly basis, new Spaces totalled 25,225 (+41.5% MoM on a base of 17,828), with Document AI the fastest-growing named use case at +48.8% MoM and enterprise productivity reaching 7.4% of new Spaces. The dashboard cautions that the large MoM figure is partly base-sensitive — August 2026 was the first full tracked month — and that the weekly run-rate of ~6.4k new Spaces per week is the cleaner read on current pace.

Total routed tokens on OpenRouter reached 717.5T in October, up +26.5% month-on-month (Sep '26 → Oct '26), with 4 providers growing volume and 4 shrinking. DeepSeek was the standout gainer at +80.3% in volume, lifting its share from 22.5% to 32.0% (+9.6pp); Anthropic surged +161.6% to lift share to 7.7% (+4.0pp), while OpenAI fell -9.4% and lost 3.9pp of share to 9.9%, and Tencent dropped -22.3% (-4.0pp to 6.4%). Per the dashboard's insights, the share rotation is toward lower-cost and open-weight models as the overall pie expands — and context on Google/Gemini shows the OpenRouter drop (Google share 4.9% → 3.7%) is a developer-routing story, not a collapse, given Alphabet Q3 2026 total revenue of $127.6B (+25% YoY).

Texas Instruments catalog pricing rose +1.3% quarter-on-quarter on a stock-weighted like-for-like index (Q2-26 → Q3-26), the exact figure being +1.32%. The dashboard carries no category-level breakdown or explanatory insights for this period. Pricing is sourced from the TI catalog via Mouser on a constant-basket methodology.

H100 cloud rental rates rose +7.9% month-to-date (Oct-26 → Nov-26 MTD) to $3.88/hr, the headline benchmark per the dashboard. GB200 was the largest mover in the opposite direction at -8.6%, while B200 added +5.6% and A100 gained +4.4%; H200 was the only other decliner at -1.2%. The dashboard carries no explanatory insights, but the move is directionally consistent with the +26.5% routed-token surge in AI demand recorded in the ai-model-intel dashboard over the same period.

Q4 '26 QTD investor-podcast coverage spanned 42 episodes across 10 shows, up from just 2 episodes in Q3 '26, with tone running 6 positive. The recurring threads new to the conversation this quarter are: the Safety vs Speed in AI Development airbags analogy, AI agents expanding into retail trading and driving smartphone upgrades, and Nubank serving 140 million customers in Latin America. This is a qualitative narrative read, not a quantitative mover — no numeric change figure is assigned.

watchList: OpenAI's OpenRouter token share fell to 9.9% (-3.9pp MoM) while Anthropic surged to 7.7% (+4.0pp MoM) — monitor whether this developer-routing shift accelerates into Q4 and whether it begins to show in AI compute list prices, which are currently flat outside DeepSeek's -18.5% cut.

Brazil system-wide credit-card NPL hit 9.96% (+0.45pp MoM, Aug '26) and Nu's own 90+ NPL reached 6.9% (+0.40pp QoQ, 2Q '26) — watch Nu's 3Q '26 filing for whether the macro deterioration is transmitting into issuer-level loss rates faster than the card-share recovery (TPV share 23.6%) can offset.

TSM was the most-sold consensus name in the latest 13F (all 5 holders trimmed, -0.89pp avg, Q1 '26 → Q2 '26) even as Taiwan supply-chain revenue rose +3.5% MoM — the divergence between fund positioning and underlying revenue momentum warrants monitoring into the next 13F filing cycle (~45 days after Q3 '26 end).

H100 rental rates rose +7.9% MoM to $3.88/hr while GB200 fell -8.6% in the same period — the next-generation GPU price compression relative to H100 appreciation is a key signal for hyperscaler capex allocation and should be tracked against Taiwan Rack/ODM revenue (+4.7% MoM) in coming months.

Power/DC Electrical revenue fell -3.6% MoM against supply-chain peers clustered around +4.3% (Aug '26 → Sep '26) — the dashboard flags this as a potential timing effect or genuine turn; the next monthly Taiwan MOPS filing will clarify whether this is a one-month anomaly or the start of a broader softening in data-centre power infrastructure.
methodNote: All figures are sourced verbatim from the client-supplied DATA object: PassMark/CPUbenchmark.net (CPU prices), Taiwan MOPS/TWSE filings (semiconductor revenue), pricepertoken.com/getdeploying.com (AI compute pricing), Graybar distributor pricing (Schneider Electric), SEC EDGAR 13F filings (fund holdings), BCB/IF.data/issuer filings (Nubank), HN/Reddit/StackExchange + SAP docs (SAP AI sentiment), TSA.gov + IATA (airline demand), Hugging Face Hub (Spaces activity), OpenRouter/UBS/SEC (AI model token usage), TI catalog via Mouser (TI chip prices), getdeploying.com (GPU cloud pricing), and investor podcasts (podcast themes); nothing has been fabricated or re-rounded.
